text:
Nothing ever started, nothing ever ended. Things have been, things shall be. There’s a little sunshine today. Few clouds cleared and I could feel the sun. Then there were clouds again: the sun’s playing hide and seek with me. I have questions: big ones. I feel comfortable living with them. There’s no intention to find answers to those questions, but just let them tag along.

Ideal weather Sunrises at around 8.00 and brightens up by 9.00. It stays the way till evening 6.00. There’s cool breeze blowing by. The sun shines nonetheless. The clouds come and go. But don’t stay the way they should. It’s sunny and cool.

I wish I were an introvert who loved solitude. Seems that I crave for human company often. Be it through sexual gratification, romantic affairs, friendship, relationships and so on.

The perceived emptiness of space and time mesmerises me. After a filling lunch of rice, sambar and uppit, I sit in front of my twenty-four inch display to write a journal entry. Listening to the ambient sounds of vehicles passing by, neighbours talking and hawkers with their loudspeakers trying to sell a thing or two; I sit and type. The VPN connection is taking forever to connect to its servers.

Another day of watching B.R Chopra’s Mahabharat. Is laziness a virtue? I try to be lazy all the time. Even with reading scriptures. I’d prefer to watch a TV series of the same instead. Why has reading books become a boring activity? Because there are no pictures in it? Or there is no movement of characters? My erstwhile habits are withering away. I spend more time wondering about things and stay there. Skills of programming, engineering etc. are fading away. I just eat, sleep and defecate. Well, I do a few home chores too, but they don’t match my skill investment. I’m slowly forgetting what I was supposed to hone. I call up Praveen, a college friend of mine for a casual chat. Career, marriage and money were the topic of discussion. I’m not interested in any of those. My emptiness is pervasive, it won’t go away. No matter how many things, people or events try to fill it. I need to make peace with my loneliness.

When I look at a thing, I keep staring at it for long. I look at the backlight of the keyboard and keep observing it for long. I look at the window and just witness it. I look at the sky and see the clouds passing by. I witness existence and remain peaceful. There’s beauty. There’s enough beauty around for a lifetime. All there is to see and listen and taste and smell and be. No matter what happens I continue to live my experience. What is pain? Physical, emotional, mental or some other? I feel and endure it. What is pleasure? An outburst of orgasm, a dopamine hit or a neurological activity for simulating neurons responsible for pleasure? My thoughts seem to disappear even before they arrive. They fade away.
Should I travel to Mysore to stay with relatives just for the sake of experiencing a better weather?

I’m amidst relatives. Feeling delirious and drowsy at the same time. Sometimes these changes are just changes that I see. I try to see through. There’s no desire to be good and better, also no desire to be bad and poor. Just want to be. Exist. Thrive. Live.

Staying at a guest house away from home with relatives. Visited Kukke Subrahmanya Temple with them for performing rites and rituals. Feeling drowsy after the evening snack and have to wake up very early tomorrow to finish the left over ceremonies as part of the ritual.

A lecture from U, S, and others yesterday made me overwhelmed with external energy. I would rather go nowhere and just sit where I am. Or maybe go to a well known place. I’ve been bombarded with opinions. I don’t feel like pandering to their expectations. Want to stay back. Sit back and be. It’s cloudy today with no sun. I am tempted to take actions, make changes, move to places, try new things and so on. However, I feel threatened by the change itself. I have been called ’dead’ by U.

I decide to go home. I await for tomorrow morning. Will I really be back at home? Not sure. As I wait…
An emotionally charged day so far.

Fashion uncensored uncut show on Z-Trendz back in 2003 was most sought after by me. It was the show that had nude women who were skimpily clad and for the first time when I hit puberty was able to see them on TV. Those videos still exist on the internet but not freely accessible. I await for some kind of login to view them. It’s been so much hassle trying to access those videos. Alexandstreet.com is one such website that has them, but access to it is only for educational institutions. I tried my best for accessing them but can’t do it now due to the imposed restrictions. It’s a bit pricey too at $150 per video.

The striving to remain awake in the afternoon by sitting in front of the computer and staring at the extra large screens, continues. I try to not think about what happened over the past week or so but I am constantly bombarded by those thoughts. I wonder what should I be doing now? Apart from reading the books that I recently purchased.

Another day spent in living the same old life. I sense the energy within me to travel. The urge to get the car repaired and go for a ride. The urge to fly in an aeroplane. I still have things to do such as: getting the Kindle fixed so that I could read e-books on it, write an email to myself regarding the books I have started to read, fix the VPN issue on the Latitude laptop, create openVPN connection on Libreboot laptop for usage (? it works well with Tor as of now) and access to that Videofashion’s Fashion Uncensored Uncut video.

And the tirade continues… I have to now go on an airplane trip just because I booked the ticket for it. Otherwise, the money would go waste. What good is it if I spend more money on something that I don’t like doing and somehow expect that it would justify the booking? I still don’t understand my tendency to act irrationally despite knowing what’s rational. Why this urge to act emotionally and irrationally and justify it? The last thing I would want is to be a romantic.

Is life just a process of finding love, happiness, wealth, and so on? Why is there doubt, melancholy, sadness, tragedy and other such things in life? What is happiness? Should my goal be pursuit of pleasure, happiness, wealth and so on? I don’t want to pursue sadness, melancholy, despair, tragedy etc. but does that mean I pursue the former? Why can’t I make up my mind and work towards the goal I’ve set for myself? When the goals are uncertain, the process is unknown, and there is so much doubt, will I be able to go through with all these?

My friend says getting married will solve my problems. But will it? It will open a pandora’s box of misery. Misery in the guise of responsibility. What is my problem anyway? Inability to find a job that I like? Find a girlfriend whom I can just have coitus with and later be by myself? Have a place of my own to stay and carryout all of these? To have a lot of friends? All of these seem a tiresome and boring activity.

Found the old analog camera in the locker - Kodak Easy Camera 35mm. Checked out the price of the film in current times. Costs Rs.1095 for a film with 36 negatives. The development of negatives would cost another 500 rupees. The effective cost per photo approximates to 43 rupees. Is it worth it? Taking photos just for the sake of nostalgia when there is a camera built in with every reasonable mobile phone that’s sold out there in the market.

Yesterday I saw a video from Alain Du Botton called ’Philosophy of Happiness’ featuring Neitzsche. It talked of going through hardships, failures etc. and facing it with courage and rise above them. The documentary featured Alain climbing the Alps in Switzerland. It’s only after reaching the top of the mountain that he could enjoy the scenic beauty around him. The spectacular and breathtaking views. It’s only when human endures and perseveres the suffering and misery to rise above it and see the bigger picture, that it adds a certain satisfaction, accomplishment and happiness to one’s life.

There’s so much hesitance to resume programming. Why don’t I take the necessary ’baby steps’ for writing programs, solving coding assignments and similar tasks? What is that I have got to lose anyway? They’re going to steal my solutions and not offer a job? Why is it so hard to find a fulfilling job? I try hard to land an opportunity in the free and open source software development field. My application for Software Heritage got rejected. Had applied for back-end developer role. The job was based in Paris.

An early morning alarm made me wake up and bruise my finger while opening the cupboard. The cupboard in which I had placed the mobile phone. It started ringing very early, as early as 7 am. I had forgotten to turn off the recurring schedule. It’s my left middle finger. The scars on it hurt a bit. Mr. Nobody is what I am. A nothing. A nobody.

I hope to find a job soon. A job based on my previous work. I will have to complete the programming challenges that are with me unsolved for about a year. There is a lot to do. I need to divide and conquer each of the complex tasks.

I give myself the task of reviving the old desktop computer that I have. The Gigabyte motherboard BIOS is bricked and to solve it I plan on flashing the BIOS externally using a programmer. I wish to use a software ’asProgrammer’ that apparently works only on Microsoft Windows. I have created a live USB for Windows 7. Now in order to install it on this laptop I will have to erase the existing OS i.e Ubuntu GNU/Linux. I don’t want to erase it as I will lose everything and recovering it from the backup I have is a tedious process. I will end up having similar packages but not the exact replica. There should be another way. Anyway, why do I care about reviving this desktop PC now? To give it to M so that he could use it? Or to give to G? Or use it myself? Well, I don’t have an answer to that. I sure was interested in recovering the data that’s on that old fat HDD.

I had to run the medical store to get band-aid for P. She had cut herself while chopping veggies for breakfast. Hated going out but seemed like a deep enough cut worth a band-aid. Argued with P for not holding on to a reserve first-aid at home. I hope the cut wasn’t deliberate - just in order to make me get out of my cave. I feel sleepy now after the breakfast. Too many thoughts ravaging my head. Always oscillating between the extremes.

I am finding myself obsessed with reviving the old desktop whose BIOS had bricked during Coreboot flashing. I can’t answer the question as to why I want the desktop back but here are few reasons that plague me:

  • It can be used by someone else who may be in need for a computer
  • I could use it for hosting a server such as Jitsi, media (videos, music, etc.)
  • It can be used to retrieve data from the old fat HDD that is not compatible with newer laptops (unless used to with a adapter that has to be purchased)

Reasons not to revive that old desktop:

  • Waste of time as it will involve a lot of trial and error to re-flash the BIOS with stock firmware
  • The desktop will take up space on the desk and eventually start catching dust as there might not be much use to it
  • Power consumption for using the desktop may be more than that of a similar compute power offering recent computer. ’With great power comes great electricity bill’

I should refrain myself from sending messages to people whom I know. Just feel that its sometimes unnecessary. Let’s keep our poetry, journals, and our saga to ourselves. There’s no need to express unless someone wants to know.

Yesterday had gone out with A for a stroll by the lake. Later went for dinner at a fancy resort and also played a game of billiards. Too much spending for a single day or should I call it too much lavishness for a single night. Drove the scooter all the way to this place about four kilometers away from where I stay. Found a missed call from U on my phone. Not sure what was the case. Anyways, I tried to send a message through Telegram but later deleted it. I wanted to help R but, I think that if chose to go along that path, I’ll put myself into situations I wish I hadn’t been in the first place. It would be better off to just not hurry in this matter. Let em’ be. There are other things to look at anyway like - finding a paying job, pursuing my current hobbies of reading, writing, hacking, gaming and so on.

I still find it hard to convince myself that I need to work for someone else for the sake of money. It’s hard to believe that I have to exchange my services for earning money and then use that money to avail other services or buy things that I am supposed to have. This is a huge hindrance for me in finding a software job. Why do I find myself so lazed out and unwilling to work towards a job or at least create a software project of my own? I sometimes wonder what is that software which is so necessary and that’s already not available there, that I should be putting my energies in building? I am unwilling to do even simple things such as flashing a BIOS using an external programmer. I keep asking the ’Why’ questions recursively and I end up not answering that the question which leads me to stop doing what I wanted to do. For example: “I want to revive my old desktop by re-flashing the bricked BIOS” “But, why do you want it to be in working condition anyway?” “Because it will be useful for doing stuff on it” “Like what? running a server, or donating it to others, wasting electricity by running a junk that’s decade old?” “I want to access the contents of the old fat HDD that’s lying around I can’t do that without the old motherboard” “Why don’t I buy an adapter to access the contents instead? Well that’s waste of money isn’t it buying thing that are unnecessary, instead of fixing things using items that are already available?” “To flash that, I will need Windows 7, another OS. I’ll have to format the existing HDD on the laptop, install Windows 7 because the BIOS software for some reason prefers Windows over the Linux counterpart” “That’s crap, I can’t get rid of this OS with all the files and installations just to get a BIOS flashed. What’s in that old HDD anyway that you so dearly want?” “I don’t know. Only when I access it that I will be able to look at the contents.” “For some reason, I want to try using that CH341a programmer, I suspect it doesn’t work at all. But I still want to make it work.”

Spent the day trying to erase BIOS on old motherboard and flash the stock ROM. Managed to read the contents of the BIOS chip using CH341a programmer on Windows7 using AsProgrammer software. But couldn’t erase, verify or write contents to the BIOS. Put the motherboard away. Now installing Guix on Latitude laptop. Just feel bored and dejected to see things not working. Also to see that I have wasted an entire day doing almost nothing. Nothing that could earn me a paycheck at the end of the month or end of the week or end of time.

Spent last two days reinstalling this OS and getting apps to work on it. I feel devoid of energy trying to restore things back to original state. Received an email from A for resuming classes for E and P starting March. I have confirmed my availability. Why am I so reluctant to study what’s necessary to get a programming gig? I wish I’d swallow Coreman’s algorithm book and digested it completely. Yesterday, I spent enjoying my day by relishing on a Biryani and a TV series. I need to bring down the number of hours spent on these or to put it the other way - “I have work towards my goal - programming, writing and so on”.

Spent half a day today window shopping for a dishwasher at nearby retail stores with D. Do I have the money to pay for a dishwasher? Perhaps, No. I can’t splurge money on such things. Spending 40K on a dishwasher is a pointless affair. Instead spend it on learning a new skill that will give a better job.

Started with those email conversations again, with BNR. I could just focus on more important things - finding a software developer job. Had a good sleep in the afternoon having eaten a sumptuous meal with Ragi balls, chicken curry and Jira rice. AK didn’t show up for the class this evening possibly because of tomorrow’s exam.

Spent the morning and a little bit of the afternoon assembling the exercise bike that G had recently bought. My back and hands are aching after the chore. Now at 6.10 PM, I am waiting Ak to join the session for Maths tutoring. Wonder if he’s going to turn up. A waste of my time, simply waiting. I have started watching this new TV series called Moonbase 8 on Voot streaming app. It seems I will spend a lot of time watching it over the next week or so. Finished watching Larry David’s ’Curb your enthusiasm’ complete series. My PSN membership will end today or tomorrow. Had spent enough time playing RDR2 online. Another time killer but sometimes pleasurable. I’m lagging behind with my studies - Algorithms CLRS, programming tasks and others. Wonder if I’ll make enough time for those.

More - ask for more. More money, more food, more happiness, more this and more that. A sense of contentment prevails as I sit through the time. Passing of time, chirpings of the bird, rustling of leaves, clickety sound of the keyboard, sleepy as I feel laid in the chair. The aroma of the cooking breakfast hits my nose as I feel the urge to go down and eat it. I have been enjoying life to the fullest through relaxation and entertainment. The toil of work beckons me only when the world expects me to toil for a greater purpose - for survival, blah and blah.

I had to move the ’Money Plant’ from the window grill inside my room to the balcony outside. Reason being: “According to Vastu, I shouldn’t grow a creeper inside the room”, as V says. “It denotes dependence on parents for everything - food, shelter, emotional support, financial support blah blah”. Now, since I have moved it out of the room to the balcony, I will become independent - both emotionally and financially. I do crave for independence and wouldn’t mind doing a silly thing such as moving the plant from one place to another. As if it would magically get me to independence. These are the kind of reasons I need to provide myself for the things I’m facing and the need to meet the aspirations that I secretly nurture. The aspiration of being independent, have enough money to sustain a living on my own as a free individual.

Time for Alain Du Botton’s philosophical meditation. I will get my white covered notebook (with custom stickers on it) and start using it for jotting down my anxieties, qualms and ambitions. Later, I am going to start looking at the work that needs attention. I wonder why do I frequently fluctuate between ’All or Nothing’ sort of thinking and its associated actions.

After reading (or at least parts of) the book ’How to be Idle?’ by Tom Hodgkinson, I have started to embrace the anti-work culture. The same anti-work culture that’s part of the SubReddit post. ’The Great Resignation’ is another phenomenon associated with this Reddit post. The eternal question that I have always and most often am confronted with is - “Why should I work for someone else for the sake of earning money?”, “Why can’t I build something of my own, be self-sufficient, self-reliant, and so on with what I have with me already?”, “Why is there is this eternal need to satisfy every desire that I have through money?”, “How can I be more frugal in my spending and usage of resources?”. I wish I were writing all these on paper, instead of using electricity. Power to run a complex computer and the LCD display consuming that power. Isn’t it a wastage? Paper and ink are more economical I’d say. Even if electricity were free of cost, should I be using it?

A long discussion in the morning with D and G over work, job, employment, income and so on. A boring exercise - this work, trying to get payment and using that to buy things. An everlasting endurance of my faculties to wander and find work.

After a lavish extended weekend, I still feel I haven’t gotten enough. Enough of what’s due to me: luxury, pleasure, adventure, sleep, relaxation and enlightenment. Lay down, shut down, don’t wake up. What is waking life? Life without the sleep or life without life? Decipher the mundane, the boring: embrace boredom. Despising boredom is a tragedy. My ephemeral stint with Wellsite contract ended yesterday. Can’t use their proprietary products and build proprietary solutions. This is the third or fourth company whom I have refused to work for because of my free/libre open source philosophy advocacy. It makes me wonder what have I contributed to the free software movement so far. When I speak of contribution I usually refer to software work - programming, testing, documentation and so on. I have refused to work a person who wanted Emacs customization before just because the code was privately hosted. What I see here with this recent contract agreement was:

  • I failed to negotiate initially for free software licensing of my work
  • Also, not being vocal about my beliefs and philosophy. Pragmatism, unfortunately hasn’t been my strengths. It may be difficult for me to proceed along the lines of business using a free software philosophy

Not sure whether I want to earn money through paid work for a profit making business.
